messages:
alex (seceng): Heads-up: we're drafting a runbook for telemetry ingestion in private deployments. Need to nail down: RBAC for the ingest SA, KMS envelope key design, and network egress constraints so customers retain isolation guarantees. pinging infra + product-sec for constraints.

maria (infra): Quick Q — do we allow egress from collector pods to our hosted KMS endpoints or require customer-managed KMS endpoints only? Some customers require no external egress. :thinking_face:

alex (seceng): Two modes: 1) Customer-managed KMS (preferred for air-gapped): we only call the customer's KMS inside their VPC via private link. 2) Redwood-managed KMS inside customer's VPC (bring-your-keyalias): we host an HSM instance in their VPC. For fully air-gapped on-prem, we support an on-host KMS shim.

jon (platform): For the RBAC side I'd propose: per-tenant service account with short-lived tokens + KMS policy that only allows Encrypt/Decrypt for a single key alias. If compromise, rotate alias and revoke SA. Also recommend write-once audit sink.

lina (product-sec): Also need to ensure every KMS use is logged to immutable audit storage, and the ingest path includes a signed event so telemetry can't be tampered with after key rotation. How do we ensure audit integrity if someone rotates keys?

alex (seceng): Make audit independent of KMS keys used for payload encryption. Key usage is logged to Cloud Audit / KMS logs; payloads go to S3/GCS with object-lock / WORM. For on-prem, we write to a separate append-only filesystem or forward logs to a customer-managed SIEM.

sre-oncall: Thinking incident: attacker gets a collector image RCE. We need a clear play: 1) revoke SA tokens 2) rotate KMS data keys 3) freeze writes to immutable store but keep read access for forensics 4) snapshot network flows. Can we automate key rotation so it doesn't break consumers?

alex (seceng): Yes — use envelope keys: rotate the data-encryption-key (DEK) frequently and keep the key-encryption-key (KEK) under HSM. Consumers read metadata that includes key version. We'll add a reconciliation job to re-encrypt backlog if necessary.

jon (platform): Example k8s annotation we used for short-lived SA tokens: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: telemetry-ingest-sa
  annotations:
    iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: telemetry-123@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
We bind a role that only allows `kms.encrypt`, `kms.decrypt` on `projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/telemetry-<tenant>` and `storage.objects.create` to the immutable bucket.

maria (infra): For network policy, restrict egress to only: customer KMS endpoint, collector aggregator (intra-VPC), and our telemetry sink. Example minimal NetworkPolicy: 
```
kind: NetworkPolicy
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: telemetry-egress-only
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: collector
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.5.0/24    # aggregator
    - to:
      - namespaceSelector:
          matchLabels:
            role: kms
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 443
```
This prevents general internet egress.

lina (product-sec): One more: enforce signed metadata on each telemetry batch `{version, dek_id, signature}`, so if a key is rotated we can detect stale/unsigned data. Also require that ingestion service verifies signature with the public key managed by product-sec.

alex (seceng): Noted. On vulnerability triage: we've got an advisory on the collector lib (CVE-2026-XYZ). Immediate step: patch container + rebuild images, push to private registry, and rotate SA + DEKs used in the last 48h. We'll add a post-rotate verification job that replays a few sample batches into a staging decryptor.

sre-oncall: Can we include this scenario in our next tabletop? Steps currently: detect, isolate (NP/CNI), revoke creds, rotate keys, forensics sweep, re-enable. Add timing SLA: creds revoked within 10m of detection, keys rotated within 2h for affected tenants.

jon (platform): I'll open a PR for the runbook with the RBAC & KMS policy snippets + NetworkPolicy examples and a CI check that validates we don't publish images with vulnerable deps. Devops-bot: can you run an automatic CVE scan on the rebuilt image once pushed?

devops-bot: CI scan queued: job 8241 — will post results in this thread when complete. :robot_face:

maria (infra): Action items: 1) PR for runbook (jon) 2) Add immutable audit sink checklist (alex) 3) NetworkPolicy templates for on-prem customers (maria) 4) Tabletop add CVE ingestion scenario (sre-oncall). I'll schedule weekly follow-up.

alex (seceng): LGTM. I'll draft the canonical KEK/DEK diagrams and add rotation playbooks. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
